content:
Life span refers to the maximum possible age a human can reach, which is a fixed biological limit (around 120 years).  
Life expectancy at birth (LEAB) is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live given current mortality rates — this is usually shorter than the maximum life span.  
Life expectancy at a specified age (LEASA) is the remaining years expected for someone who has already reached a certain age; it will be shorter than LEAB for ages beyond infancy because the individual has already survived the earlier higher-risk years.  

Since life span is the maximum possible duration of life, it is always the longest among these concepts.  

Final answer: (B)
